question: A team is building a real-time customer support chat widget that must respond in under a second, at high volume, on a tight budget, but still needs solid reasoning quality. Which model should they start with?
options: A) Claude Fable 5, for the largest context window and always-on adaptive thinking
B) Claude Sonnet 5, for frontier intelligence at a moderate cost and speed
C) Claude Haiku 4.5, for near-frontier reasoning at the fastest, most economical tier
D) Claude Opus 4.8, for the deepest reasoning on complex agentic coding tasks
correct_answers: C) Claude Haiku 4.5, for near-frontier reasoning at the fastest, most economical tier
explanations: Incorrect. Claude Fable 5 is built for long-running agents with large context needs and is priced and latency-tuned for a very different workload than a real-time chat widget.
Incorrect. Sonnet 5 is fast and capable, but it costs and latencies more than necessary for a simple, high-volume support widget compared to Haiku 4.5.
Correct. Claude Haiku 4.5 is positioned as the fastest, most economical model with near-frontier intelligence, matching real-time, high-volume, cost-sensitive chat requirements.
Incorrect. Opus 4.8 targets complex agentic coding and enterprise work at moderate latency and higher cost, which is more than this low-latency, high-volume workload needs.
